o1.biggest_strength: Uses the real numbers to drive decisions (niacinamide's 8% vs sunscreen's 2.2%, 44% dark spots, 61% new to actives) and the conditional product matching plus sunscreen-doubt email directly answers Sneha's and Arjun's fears.
o1.biggest_mistake: Runs slightly long (the tests/projection section and per-click revenue math push past the 1,800-word brief) and the product-match logic lumps in 'no answer' with dark spots, which could mis-aim some subscribers.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Trim the projected-revenue and A/B math to fit the word limit, and make the 'no answer' path a gentle 'tell us your concern' nudge rather than defaulting to niacinamide.

o2.biggest_strength: Clean, calm, on-brand copy with clear three-version personalisation and a well-placed sunscreen-questions email; easy to read and close to sendable.
o2.biggest_mistake: Email 5 pushes a fixed 3-step routine (wash + niacinamide + sunscreen together) that contradicts the brand's own 'one active at a time, start slowly' rule and ignores each person's quiz answer; the WhatsApp also lacks a concrete product pick.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the closing email follow the quiz answer with a two-step routine and a starter pick, and keep the 'add one at a time' teaching consistent with it.

reason: Both are good and on-brand, but Output 1 reads the data harder (why sunscreen clicks don't convert, the 8% vs 2.2% gap) and ties every email to a fixed job and product match, while Output 2's final routine breaks its own start-slow advice and slightly bends the facts (a 3-step routine with an acid wash twice a day).
